A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same min-p sampling study, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D. The material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original GPQA and GSM8K experiments, accuracy-diversity analyses, and human evaluations in Sections 5-6 and Appendices B-C.

after.justification: v7 retains these original benchmark experiments, analyses, and human evaluation results.

M1.justification: The threshold pbase times pmax, token filtering, renormalization, sampling procedure, and temperature ordering are unchanged. Appendix A.1 retains the same implementation; the new contrastive-decoding discussion does not modify min-p.

E1.justification: Both versions retain GPQA, GSM8K including self-consistency, AlpacaEval creative writing, human story evaluations, and constrained creative generation in Appendix C.3. EQ-Bench results were already discussed in v5.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments, including top-p, top-k, temperature-only, epsilon/eta sampling, Mirostat, and appendix sampler variants. Newly cited contrastive decoding is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Prompting, model configurations, temperature grids, metrics, judges, and survey designs are retained. The switch to vLLM and other refinements described in Appendix C.2 already appeared in v5.

E4.justification: The temperature and threshold sweeps, combined-sampler tests, token case studies, accuracy-diversity analysis, and supplementary evaluations are unchanged. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same confidence intervals, standard errors, significance conventions, paired-test description, and seed/run information. There is no new uncertainty-reporting practice or reported increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains GPQA accuracy of 26.34% for min-p and 6.47% for top-p at temperature 2.0.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(3) and the formulas in Appendix D.2 are unchanged. The added prior-work formula restates the existing maximum-probability scaling principle; it introduces no new derivation, assumption, or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about novelty, quality-diversity benefits, high-temperature performance, cross-model applicability, human preference, and community adoption.

C2.justification: Interpretations of confidence-sensitive filtering, accuracy-diversity tradeoffs, computational behavior, and human-study limitations are retained. Appendix D.2 preserves the same applicability boundaries and future-research qualifications.

D1.justification: Implementation code, hyperparameter-selection guidance, hardware/runtime disclosures, survey and judge procedures, and project-access information remain unchanged. Splitting the code listing across pages adds no technical information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Li et al. (2023a), acknowledging a similar adaptive plausibility threshold and distinguishing standalone min-p sampling from expert/amateur contrastive decoding. Paech (2024) is also added for EQ-Bench. These are focused additions to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v7 adds one related-work paragraph, renames 'Computational Efficiency' to 'Simplicity,' repairs the unresolved EQ-Bench citation, and adjusts citation labels and bibliography formatting. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Text reflow changes placement around existing figures and tables, and Appendix A.1's code listing now spans pages 16-17. Figures, table structures, axes, legends, and captions are retained; pages 20-34 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v7 improves attribution by explicitly relating min-p to the earlier adaptive plausibility constraint and repairing the missing EQ-Bench citation. Some existing references lose venue and full-URL text, but retain titles and DOIs. The clearer positioning provides a limited net improvement, with methodology and empirical support unchanged.
